sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, manager_id, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all requests for a given employee; status: filtering by pending/approved/rejected for manager dashboards and approval queues; leave_type: filtering requests by type (annual, sick, emergency); start_date, end_date: range queries for overlapping leave detection and calendar views; (employee_id, status): compound lookup for 'my pending requests' queries

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, year, total_allocated, used, pending, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups of balances for a specific employee; (employee_id, leave_type_id, year): unique constraint and primary access pattern — 'what is my annual leave balance for 2025?'; leave_type_id: aggregating balances by leave type across employees
table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, is_paid, created_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name (annual, sick, emergency)

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_id, max_days_per_year, max_consecutive_days, requires_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: lookup of policy by leave type; is_active: filtering active policies

table audit_logs | fields: id, employee_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, changes, created_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups of audit records by employee; action: filtering by action type (created, approved, rejected); created_at: time-range queries for audit reports

methods: findOverlapping(employeeId: string, startDate: Date, endDate: Date): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>
updateStatus(id: string, status: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest>
findByEmployeeTypeYear(employeeId: string, leaveTypeId: string, year: number): Promise<LeaveBalance | null>
deductPending(employeeId: string, leaveTypeId: string, year: number, days: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>
restorePending(employeeId: string, leaveTypeId: string, year: number, days: number, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveBalance>

data_notes: leave_balances uses a (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) unique constraint to ensure one balance row per employee per leave type per year. The `pending` field tracks days requested but not yet approved/rejected — deducted on submission, restored on rejection, moved to `used` on approval. The `used` field tracks days actually consumed from approved requests. `total_allocated` is set from leave_policies.max_days_per_year when the balance row is first created for a year. audit_logs is a shared table referenced by all modules per GP-002; its schema is defined here once and referenced by name elsewhere.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — calendar days or business days (Mon–Fri excluding holidays)?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance deduction arithmetic in every write path (submit, approve, reject) and the overlapping-detection query. If calendar days, a Friday–Monday leave consumes 4 days; if business days, it consumes 2.
candidate_options: calendar_days: count every day in [start_date, end_date] inclusive
business_days: count Mon–Fri only, excluding weekends
business_days_with_holidays: count Mon–Fri minus a holiday calendar table

transaction_contract: Repository methods that participate in multi-step writes (create, updateStatus, upsert, deductPending, restorePending, create audit) accept an optional `client?: PoolClient` parameter. When `client` is provided, the method uses it for all queries within that call instead of the shared pool. The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes `BEGIN`, passes the client to every repository call in the operation, then executes `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`. When `client` is omitted, the repository method uses the shared pool directly (suitable for single-step reads or single-write operations).
